Project Overview
Objective: Develop a system that uses transformer models to analyze
network traffic and system logs to detect anomalies and predict
potential cybersecurity threats before they occur.
Technical Problem Solved: Improves security posture by proactively
identifying and mitigating risks, reducing the likelihood of successful
cyber attacks.
Project Breakdown
1. Project Planning
Define Scope: Decide whether to focus on network traffic analysis,
system log analysis, or both.
Identify Data Sources: Determine where you'll get the data (e.g.,
simulated network traffic, open-source datasets).
Set Goals: Establish what types of threats you aim to detect (e.g.,
malware, DDoS attacks, insider threats).
2. Tech Stack Selection
Frontend:
Framework: React.js or Angular for building a responsive user
interface.
Visualization Libraries: D3.js or Chart.js for data visualization.

performance.

2. MOOCs at Poornima University:  
 
MOOCs envelops best in class teaching - learning processes along with meeting the requirements of various 
courses in terms of quality of t eaching and evaluation system. To promote the MOOCs among students of 
Poornima University, it is decided to consider the credits earned through MOOCs.

platforms)  
 Credit and Non -credit SWAYAM MOOCs can be opted by anyone, anytime, anywhere and in any language. 
However, prior -permission of the University Authorities is mandatory if the credits are to be transferred to 
regular degree.  
 In case of credit courses, there are two ways to opt these courses for the purpose of credit transfer to PU system

OPTION–I: As Open Elective (for batches entered till 2022) / Multidisciplinary Courses (for 
batches admitted  from 2023 -24 onwards):   
 
Open Elective (for batches entered till 2022) / Multidisciplinary Courses (for batches admitted from 2023 -24 
onwards) are available at University level in offline mode for which relevant booklets are already published. 
These cours es carries 02 credits.  These category/type of courses (similar/different) are also available as MOOC 
courses. The respective Deans / HODs shall provide both the options to all the students to either select offline 
courses or MOOCs as per details given belo w: 
 Deans / HODs shall prepare a list of upto 05 appropriate MOOC courses of 02/03 credits each, well in advance 
(at-least 15 days prior to commencement of semester) and take approval from the Office of Dean, Academics / 
Pro-President, PU.

(b) Important points related to MOOCs at Poornima University  
 Only one MOOC shall be allowed in a particular semester for the purpose of credit transfer in the beginning.  
 No attendance will be taken for MOOC courses.  
 Last period of T/T/S shall be taken for MOOC courses which shall be in self -study mode.  
 The method of  assessments of MOOC such as assignments and examination are completely associated with that 
particular MOOC and no exam will be conducted by the department as well as by the Examination Cell.  
 The respective Dean / HOD must submit the detail of course i.e. , code, name and credit of MOOC opted against 
that particular course in particular semester attached with highlighting in the related examination scheme of 
syllabus of that semester signed by BOS Convener / HoD and Dean of Faculty to the office of Pro -President 
before commencement of the classes.
doc_312aa3ff_chunk_23:

center of examination for SWAYAM MOOCs will be finalized by SWAYAM. All the responsibility related to 
registration for MOOCs, timely submission of assignments, examinations etc. will be borne by the students only.  
 The list of registered students in MOOC along with name of course will be submitted to the Examination Cell by 
the Deans / HoDs before commencemen t of the classes.  
 Any student who would not be able to register/present/clear/pass the MOOC in the stipulated time, it is the

BARCAR1101  HISTORY  OF ARCHITECTURE  – I 2 Credits  [LTP:  2-0-0] 
 
A. OBJECTIVE  
Study of the history of archite cture is a very important aspect. It deals with the development  from 
ancient to medieval to modern. It gives an idea about the technology, society, culture,  materials  used 
etc. in the ancient  time,  then in the modern  era. 
 
B. COURSE  OUTCOME  
 To illustrate  art & architecture  of ancient  civilizations.

Social  M edia  AI  Autom ation  System :  The  
Ultim ate  Build  Guide
Comprehensive 15 Day Implementation Manual for n8n, 
Supabase, and Gemini
This document serves as the complete technical blueprint for building a modular and client 
safe social media automation system. We have expanded every section to provide granular 
detail on node conﬁgurations, database schemas, and AI prompting strategies.
Project Foundation and Strategy
The goal of this system is to remove the manual burden of content creation while keeping 
the client ﬁrmly in control of their brand voice. By using n8n as the orchestrator, Supabase 
as the brain, and Gemini as the creative engine, we create a professional grade tool that 
rivals expensive SaaS platforms.
The 15 Day Execution Timeline
Day 1 to 3: Environment setup, Supabase schema design, and Brand Onboarding ﬂows.
Day 4 to 6: AI Content Engine development using Gemini for captions and OpenAI for image 
prompts.
doc_1fc3d34a_chunk_1:
Day 1 to 3: Environment setup, Supabase schema design, and Brand Onboarding ﬂows.
Day 4 to 6: AI Content Engine development using Gemini for captions and OpenAI for image 
prompts.
Day 7 to 9: WhatsApp Approval System integration and response handling logic.
Day 10 to 12: Multi platform publishing via Graph API and Cron scheduling.
Day 13 to 15: Logging, Analytics, Error handling, and Final Client Handover.
BLOCK 1: Brand Onboarding and Database Architecture
In this block, we build the infrastructure that allows the AI to "remember" who it is writing 
for. Without a solid database, the AI will produce generic content. We use Supabase 
because it handles relational data and provides a great API for n8n.
Detailed Supabase Schema
We need several tables to keep things organized. Here is the expanded SQL structure:
1. Brands Table
doc_1fc3d34a_chunk_2:
This table stores the core identity of each client.
•id: uuid (primary key)
•brand name: text
•industry: text
•target audience: text
•tone of voice: text (e.g., professional, witty, aggressive)
•forbidden words: text (comma separated list)
•brand colors: text
•created at: timestamp
2. Content Calendar Table
This tracks every single post from idea to publication.
•id: uuid
•brand id: uuid (foreign key)
•planned date: date
•topic: text
•status: text (options: pending, generated, approved, rejected, published)
•platform: text (e.g., Instagram, LinkedIn)
3. Drafts Table
Where the AI outputs live before they are approved.
•id: uuid
•calendar id: uuid
•caption version a: text
•caption version b: text
•image prompt: text
•hashtags: text
•gemini model version: text
The Onboarding Webhook Flow
The onboarding ﬂow is an n8n workﬂow that starts with a Webhook node. This is where the 
client or account manager submits the brand details.
doc_1fc3d34a_chunk_3:
1.Webhook Node: Receives a JSON payload with brand info.
2.Data Validation Node: Uses a Code node to ensure all required ﬁelds (name, tone, 
industry) are present.
3.Supabase Insert Node: Creates the brand record.
4.AI Strategy Node: A Gemini call that takes the raw brand info and generates a "Brand 
Bible" summary to be used in future prompts.
5.Conﬁrmation Node: Sends a message back to the user conﬁrming the brand is ready for 
automation.
BLOCK 2: The AI Content Generation Engine
This is the heart of the system. We are using Gemini for the heavy lifting of writing because 
of its large context window and OpenAI for speciﬁc tasks like image prompt engineering.
Advanced Prompt Engineering Strategy
We dont just ask the AI to "write a post." We use a structured prompt that includes the 
brand voice rules.
The System Prompt Template
"You are a professional social media manager for [Brand Name]. Your industry is [Industry]. 
Your target audience is [Audience]. Your tone must be [Tone].
doc_1fc3d34a_chunk_4:
The System Prompt Template
"You are a professional social media manager for [Brand Name]. Your industry is [Industry]. 
Your target audience is [Audience]. Your tone must be [Tone].
Rules:
1.Never use these words: [Forbidden Words].
2.Always include a call to action.
3.Keep captions under 200 words.
4.Generate two versions: Version A is direct and informative, Version B is storytelling and 
engaging."
n8n Workﬂow Steps for Generation
1.Cron Trigger: Runs every Sunday to generate the next weeks content.
2.Supabase Select: Grabs the brand rules and the planned topics for the week.
3.Split In Batches: Processes each post topic one by one.
4.Gemini Node (Captions): Uses the system prompt to generate A/B versions.
doc_1fc3d34a_chunk_5:
5.OpenAI Node (Image Prompts): Takes the approved topic and generates a detailed DALL-
E 3 style prompt for the visual team.
6.OpenAI Node (Hashtags): Generates 15 relevant hashtags based on the caption content.
7.Supabase Update: Saves all these details into the Drafts table.
Multi Language Logic
If the client needs content in multiple languages, we add a "Language" ﬁeld to the Brands 
table. The n8n ﬂow then adds a "Translate to [Language]" instruction to the Gemini prompt. 
This makes the system ready for global scaling from day one.
BLOCK 3: The WhatsApp Approval System
A common mistake in automation is "set it and forget it." We prevent this by putting a 
human in the loop via WhatsApp.
The Approval Interface
We use the WhatsApp Business API (or a provider like Twilio or Wati) to send the drafts to 
the client.
1.Draft Ready Trigger: An n8n ﬂow monitors the Drafts table for new entries.
2.WhatsApp Message Node: Sends a message like this:
"New Content Ready for [Brand Name]!
doc_1fc3d34a_chunk_6:
the client.
1.Draft Ready Trigger: An n8n ﬂow monitors the Drafts table for new entries.
2.WhatsApp Message Node: Sends a message like this:
"New Content Ready for [Brand Name]!
Topic: [Topic]
Version A: [Caption A]
Version B: [Caption B]
Hashtags: [Hashtags]
Reply with:
1 to Approve A
2 to Approve B
3 to Reject
4 to Edit"
Response Handling Logic
When the client replies, another n8n webhook catches the message.
doc_1fc3d34a_chunk_7:
•If "1" or "2": The system updates the status to "approved" and sets the "ﬁnal caption" 
column in Supabase.
•If "3": The status is set to "rejected," and a notiﬁcation is sent to the content team.
•If "4": The system asks the client to type their edits, which are then saved back to the 
draft for a ﬁnal check.
This ensures that no post ever goes live without a literal thumbs up from the client.
BLOCK 4: Multi Platform Publishing and Scheduling
Once approved, the content needs to get out there. We focus on Instagram ﬁrst but build it 
so you can add LinkedIn or Twitter easily.
Instagram Graph API Integration
To post to Instagram, you need a Facebook Developer account and an Access Token.
1.The Scheduler: A Cron node runs every hour.
2.Check for Approved: It queries Supabase for any post where "status = approved" and 
"planned date <= current time."
3.Media Upload: Since Instagram requires a URL for the image, the system ﬁrst ensures
doc_1fc3d34a_chunk_8:
"planned date <= current time."
3.Media Upload: Since Instagram requires a URL for the image, the system ﬁrst ensures 
the image is hosted (using a tool like Cloudinary or S3).
4.Graph API Post: A HTTP Request node sends the ﬁnal caption and image URL to the 
Instagram container endpoint.
5.Publishing: A second API call is made to actually "publish" the container.
Failure Retry and Logging
APIs fail sometimes. We add an Error Trigger in n8n.
•If a post fails, the system waits 1 hour and tries again.
•After 3 failed attempts, it sends an urgent WhatsApp message to the admin.
•Every successful post ID is saved back to Supabase so we have a permanent record of 
what went live.
BLOCK 5: Logging, Analytics and Continuous Learning
The ﬁnal phase is about making the system smarter. We don't just post; we analyze.
doc_1fc3d34a_chunk_9:
Analytics Logging
We create a table in Supabase called "Analytics."
•post id: uuid
•likes: integer
•comments: integer
•shares: integer
•reach: integer
An n8n workﬂow runs every 24 hours to fetch these stats via the Graph API and update the 
table.
The Weekly Learning Loop
At the end of each week, we run a "Learning Workﬂow."
1.Summarize Stats: Gemini looks at the top 3 performing posts and the bottom 3.
2.Extract Insights: It identiﬁes what worked (e.g., "shorter captions got more likes").
3.Update Brand Voice: The system automatically appends these "lessons learned" to the 
Brand Rules in Supabase.
4.Feedback Capture: We also store the clients "Rejection Reasons" from Phase 3 to make 
sure the AI stops making the same mistakes.
Technical Requirements and Build Rules
To keep this project safe and professional, we follow these strict rules:
1.Modularity: Every phase is a separate n8n workﬂow. This prevents one error from 
breaking the whole system.
doc_1fc3d34a_chunk_10:
To keep this project safe and professional, we follow these strict rules:
1.Modularity: Every phase is a separate n8n workﬂow. This prevents one error from 
breaking the whole system.
2.Security: No API keys are written inside the nodes. We use the n8n Credentials system or 
Environment Variables.
3.Logging: Every AI step has a "Log" node before and after it to record exactly what was 
sent and received.
4.Clear Documentation: Every node is named according to its function (e.g., "Supabase: 
Get Brand Tone" instead of just "Supabase").
Deliverables for the Client
doc_1fc3d34a_chunk_11:
At the end of the 15 days, the client receives:
1.The Master n8n Workﬂow Files (JSON).
2.The Supabase Database Access.
3.A User Manual on how to use the WhatsApp Approval system.
4.A Dashboard (built in Supabase or a tool like Softr) showing the content calendar and 
analytics.
This system represents a full scale AI agency in a box, ready to handle dozens of clients with 
minimal human intervention.
Deep Dive: BLOCK 1 - Advanced Brand Onboarding and 
Data Architecture
The onboarding process is more than just a form; it is a strategic discovery phase. To 
achieve a 15 day timeline, we must automate the collection of brand assets and rules.
Detailed Database Schema Expansion
Beyond the basic tables, we need to handle media and competitor data.
4. Media Assets Table
This table stores the URLs of brand logos, preferred stock images, and client uploaded 
videos.
•id: uuid
•brand id: uuid
•asset url: text

5. Competitor Analysis Table

The Apify Integration for Competitor Analysis
To make the AI smarter, we use Apify to scrape competitor social media pages.
1.Input: The client provides 3 competitor handles during onboarding.
2.Apify Actor: An n8n node triggers an Apify actor (like the Instagram Scraper).
3.Data Processing: We extract the captions and engagement metrics of the competitors 
last 10 posts.
4.Gemini Analysis: Gemini reviews this data and identiﬁes "content gaps" (topics the 
competitors are missing).
5.Strategy Storage: These insights are saved to the Brands table to inform future content 
generation.
Deep Dive: BLOCK 2 - Advanced Content Generation 
Workﬂows
Generating content is easy; generating content that converts is hard. We use a multi step 
"Think-Write-Review" chain.
Step 1: The "Think" Phase (Topic Research)
Before writing a caption, Gemini acts as a researcher.
•Prompt: "Given the current date (Feb 2026) and the brand industry (Tech), what are the
doc_1fc3d34a_chunk_14:
Step 1: The "Think" Phase (Topic Research)
Before writing a caption, Gemini acts as a researcher.
•Prompt: "Given the current date (Feb 2026) and the brand industry (Tech), what are the 
trending topics? Cross reference this with the competitors gaps we identiﬁed."
•Output: A list of 5 high potential topics for the week.
Step 2: The "Write" Phase (Drafting)
We use Gemini 1.5 Pro for this step due to its high reasoning capability.
•We pass the entire "Brand Bible" (from Phase 1) into the context window.
•We request the A/B versions as mentioned, but we also ask for "Platform Speciﬁc 
Formatting" (e.g., line breaks for Instagram, professional structure for LinkedIn).
Step 3: The "Review" Phase (Self Correction)
We use a second AI call (OpenAI GPT 4o) to review Geminis work.
doc_1fc3d34a_chunk_15:
•Prompt: "Act as a strict brand editor. Does this caption follow the tone rules? Are there 
any forbidden words? If yes, rewrite it. If no, pass it through."
•This "Dual Model Review" signiﬁcantly reduces the number of rejections from the client 
in Phase 3.
Deep Dive: BLOCK 3 - The WhatsApp Approval Engine in 
Detail
The WhatsApp approval system is the primary touchpoint for the client. It must be 
frictionless.
Handling Multiple Brands
If you are running an agency, the system must know which client is replying. We use the 
"Phone Number" as the unique identiﬁer in Supabase.
1.Incoming Message: Webhook receives the phone number and the message text.
2.Lookup: n8n searches the Brands table for the owner of that phone number.
3.Context Retrieval: It ﬁnds the most recent "pending" draft for that brand.
4.Action: It applies the approval or rejection to that speciﬁc draft.
The "Edit" Workﬂow
If a client replies with "4" (Edit), the system enters an "Edit Mode."
doc_1fc3d34a_chunk_16:
4.Action: It applies the approval or rejection to that speciﬁc draft.
The "Edit" Workﬂow
If a client replies with "4" (Edit), the system enters an "Edit Mode."
•n8n sends a message: "Please type your changes below."
•The system waits for the next message from that number.
•It takes the new text and uses Gemini to merge the clients edits with the original brand 
voice.
•It sends the updated version back for a ﬁnal "Yes/No" approval.
Deep Dive: BLOCK 4 - Mastering the Graph API for 
Publishing
Publishing via the Graph API can be tricky due to permission scopes and media

Error Handling and System Resilience
In a 15 day build, you must account for what happens when things go wrong.
The "Dead Letter" Workﬂow
If any node in any workﬂow fails, it triggers the "Global Error Handler."
•It logs the error message, the node name, and the timestamp.
•It checks the severity. If it is a "Publishing Failure," it pings the admin on WhatsApp 
immediately.
•If it is a "Generation Failure," it simply retries the node after 5 minutes.
Rate Limit Management
APIs like Gemini and OpenAI have rate limits.
•We use the "Wait" node in n8n to space out requests.
•We use "Batches" of 5 posts at a time to avoid hitting limits during the weekly 
generation phase.

Row Level Security (RLS) in Supabase
Security is paramount. You cannot have Client A accidentally seeing Client B's content. We 
implement RLS policies on every table.
1.Authentication: Every client is given a unique login to the dashboard.
2.Policy: CREATE POLICY "Clients can only see their own data" ON content_drafts FOR ALL USING 
(brand_id IN (SELECT id FROM brands WHERE owner_id = auth.uid()));
3.This ensures that even if there is a bug in the n8n ﬂow, the database itself will block any 
unauthorized data access.
The n8n "Master Controller" Workﬂow
Instead of having 50 identical workﬂows, we use a "Master Controller" pattern.
•One workﬂow triggers every hour.
•It fetches a list of all active brands from Supabase.
